H1_elite_bias.title: H1: Elite reviewers rate differently from never-elite users
H1_elite_bias.null_hypothesis: Reviews written by Elite users (in their elite years) and by never-elite users have the same mean and variance of stars.
H1_elite_bias.test: Welch t-test (means), Levene (variances), Mann-Whitney U on per-user means (robustness)
H1_elite_bias.conclusion: Elite reviews average 3.98 stars vs 3.68 for never-elite users (higher; Welch p < 1e-300; Cohen's d = 0.21, a small effect). Elite ratings are less spread out (SD 1.05 vs 1.58; Levene p < 1e-300): 3.33% are 1-star vs 18.98%, and 37.75% are 5-star vs 48.9%. The per-user test (one mean per user, p = 0.545) disagrees, so the review-level result should be read with care.

H2_city_category.title: H2: Average ratings differ between cities and between categories
H2_city_category.null_hypothesis: Mean review stars are equal across the 10 largest cities (and across the 12 largest categories).
H2_city_category.test: One-way ANOVA + Kruskal-Wallis; effect size eta squared
H2_city_category.conclusion: Among the 10 largest cities, Santa Barbara has the highest mean (4.01) and Tucson the lowest (3.71). The difference is statistically significant (ANOVA p < 1e-300, Kruskal-Wallis p < 1e-300); city explains 0.35% of rating variance. Category explains more (0.91% of variance): Active Life is rated highest (4.01) and Event Planning & Services lowest (3.33).

H3_length_usefulness.title: H3: Longer reviews receive more 'useful' votes
H3_length_usefulness.null_hypothesis: There is no monotonic association between review length and useful votes.
H3_length_usefulness.test: Spearman rank correlation; Mann-Whitney U (elite vs never-elite length)
H3_length_usefulness.conclusion: Review length and useful votes have a moderate positive rank correlation (Spearman rho = 0.34, p < 1e-300). Elite reviews are longer than never-elite ones (median 664 vs 349 characters; one-sided Mann-Whitney p < 1e-300). Lower-star reviews tend to be longer: complaints are written in more detail (rho stars~length = -0.22).
